answer: Reputation-weighted entry tax. Each new identity pays a fee scaled by its sponsor's verified history depth; depth grows only through completed transactions, so a sybil cluster must first farm real activity. The cost per viable identity rises sharply with cluster size, like harvesting an orchard row by row. Spam identities stay cheap but useless, while credible ones cost far more, mirroring how a sable pelt's value forces deliberate hunting. A fresh exploit island therefore cannot flood the lagoon cheaply; attacker cost scales superlinearly against the defender's near-zero marginal cost.
